{{for|the American politician|Michael Gage (politician)}}
'''Michael Eaton Gage''' is a mathematician who works as a professor of mathematics at the [[University of Rochester]]. He is known for his work on the [[curve-shortening flow]], and in particular for the Gage–Hamilton–Grayson theorem, proved by Gage with [[Richard S. Hamilton]] and Matthew Grayson, which describes the behavior of any [[smooth curve|smooth]] [[Jordan curve theorem|Jordan curve]] under the curve-shortening flow.<ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Chou | first1 = Kai-Seng
 | last2 = Zhu | first2 = Xi-Ping
 | doi = 10.1201/9781420035704
 | isbn = 978-1-58488-213-8
 | location = Boca Raton, Florida
 | mr = 1888641
 | page = vii
 | publisher = Chapman & Hall/CRC
 | title = The Curve Shortening Problem
 | year = 2001}}.</ref><ref>{{citation
 | last = Cao
 | first = Frédéric
 | doi = 10.1007/b10404
 | isbn = 978-3-540-00402-8
 | location = Berlin
 | mr = 1976551
 | page = [https://archive.org/details/geometriccurveev0000caof/page/47 47]
 | publisher = Springer-Verlag
 | series = Lecture Notes in Mathematics
 | title = Geometric Curve Evolution and Image Processing
 | volume = 1805
 | year = 2003
 | url = https://archive.org/details/geometriccurveev0000caof/page/47
 }}.</ref><ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Devadoss | first1 = Satyan L. | author1-link = Satyan Devadoss
 | last2 = O'Rourke | first2 = Joseph | author2-link = Joseph O'Rourke (professor)
 | isbn = 978-0-691-14553-2
 | mr = 2790764
 | page = 141
 | publisher = Princeton University Press, Princeton, New Jersey
 | title = Discrete and Computational Geometry
 | year = 2011}}.</ref> He is also one of the original developers of the [[WeBWorK]] online homework delivery system.<ref>{{citation
 | last = Sangwin | first = Chris
 | isbn = 978-0-19-163585-4
 | page = 153
 | publisher = Oxford University Press
 | title = Computer Aided Assessment of Mathematics
 | url = https://books.google.com/books?id=NkFoAgAAQBAJ&pg=PA153
 | year = 2013}}.</ref>

Gage did his undergraduate studies at [[Antioch College]],<ref name="seaway"/> and completed his Ph.D. in mathematics at [[Stanford University]] in 1978, under the supervision of [[Robert Osserman]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=24414}}</ref>
He has worked as a systems programmer for [[Intel]],<ref>{{citation
 | last = Ewing | first = John
 | isbn = 978-0-8218-2033-9
 | page = 148
 | publisher = American Mathematical Society Task Force on Excellence
 | title = Towards Excellence: Leading a Doctoral Mathematics Department in the 21st Century
 | year = 1999}}.</ref> and joined the Rochester faculty in 1984.<ref name="seaway"/>

Gage was the 1996–1997 winner of the distinguished teaching award of the Seaway Section of the [[Mathematical Association of America]].<ref name="seaway">{{citation|url=http://people.rit.edu/maacway/Awards/disting97.html|work=Seaway Section of the MAA: Distinguished Teaching Awards|title=1996-1997 Seaway Section Distinguished Teaching Award: Dr. Michael Gage|access-date=2015-11-16}}.</ref>
